patients.summary: Administrative assistant with chronic hypertension on labetalol and class I obesity who joins the practice two months after her first cesarean. Her 2024 pregnancy brings an antepartum admission for bleeding, superimposed preeclampsia and magnesium toxicity before a 34-week repeat cesarean; her 2026 pregnancy ends with severe preeclampsia of the HELLP form and a postpartum magnesium toxicity readmission, known to the practice only through records after her last visit in September 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

32 yo woman establishing care. Her OB asked her to find a primary doctor for her blood pressure now that she is about 9 weeks out from delivery. Cesarean in early February 2023, recovered fine, baby doing well. BP was found high during that pregnancy and OB started labetalol 200 mg BID; she has stayed on it since. Still taking her prenatal with DHA daily. Home cuff readings she brought: mostly low 130s over mid 80s. No headaches, vision change, chest pain or swelling.

PMH: chronic hypertension; obesity.
PSH: lap cholecystectomy 2019; C-section Feb 2023.
Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID; prenatal vitamin w/ DHA daily.
Allergies: none known.
Family: mother had preeclampsia and delivered early. Father on treatment for high blood pressure. Maternal grandmother had a stroke.
Social: married, works as an administrative assistant. Never smoked, no alcohol.
Prior care: OB and a previous primary office; records requested. She reports a normal Pap in 2022.

Exam: BP as charted, a bit above goal. Well appearing. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed low transverse incision and port scars. No edema.
BMI in the class I obesity range.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. Chronic HTN - near goal on labetalol, which is reasonable while she may want more children. Continue 200 mg BID, keep home log. Recheck BP with nurse in a month.
2. Obesity - talked about walking at lunch and portion sizes; she is interested.
3. Health maintenance - baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, TSH, urine microalbumin. One-time HIV and hep C screens, she agrees.
RTC 4 months.

documents.body: Hi Tiana, all of your labs came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, sugar (A1c), thyroid and urine protein. HIV and hepatitis C screens negative. Nothing to change. See you for the BP check next month.

documents.title: Positive pregnancy test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. Took a home test this weekend and it was positive. Last period started July 11. A little sooner than we planned but we're happy. Should I keep taking the labetalol? I already have a call in to my OB.

documents.title: RE: Positive pregnancy test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Yes, keep taking the labetalol 200 mg twice a day. It is one of the preferred blood pressure medicines in pregnancy. Keep the prenatal vitamin too. Your OB will take the lead on the pregnancy and I am happy to help with blood pressure along the way. Please send me your home readings every couple of weeks, and call right away for a reading of 160/110 or higher, a bad headache, or vision changes.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT / OBSTETRIC TRIAGE
Date of service: 01/22/2024

33F G2P1 at 27w6d by early dating, prior cesarean. Arrived with bright vaginal bleeding that started about an hour before arrival, painless. Pregnancy had been going smoothly. Baby moving normally. Denies any trauma, fever, belly pain, cramping or contractions, or fluid leaking. No intercourse recently.

Hx: chronic hypertension, obesity. Surgical: cesarean 2023, lap chole 2019.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; labetalol 200 mg BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother - preeclampsia, early delivery; father - HTN; MGM - CVA.
SH: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: anxious appearing, vitals stable. Abdomen gravid, soft, not tender.
FHR: baseline 140, moderate variability, no decels.
Sterile speculum: blood pooled in the vault. Digital cervical exam NOT performed - contraindicated until placental location established.

Plan: obstetric ultrasound ordered. OB on call consulted at bedside. Admitted to the antepartum unit under obstetrics. No digital cervical checks.

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just letting you know I'm admitted to the hospital for bleeding. They say I'll probably be here until the baby comes. BP has been ok. I'll have to miss whatever I had scheduled with you.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thank you for letting us know, Tiana. We received the ER record. Your doctor sends best wishes. Nothing was booked with us yet. Call us once you're home and we'll get you in to check your BP.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 business days after discharge (home 3/10 after C-section 3/6 at 34 wks). Baby still in the nursery at the hospital, she visits daily. Incision sore, improving, no redness or drainage. Home BPs 130s-140s/80s-90s. No headache, vision change, SOB or swelling. Taking labetalol BID and her prenatal. Discharge summary not yet received; requested. Visit booked 3/19 with PCP.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - OBSTETRICS
Admitted 01/22/2024   Discharged 03/10/2024

Reason for admission: painless vaginal bleeding at 27w6d in a patient with a prior cesarean. Admitted from the ED for antepartum observation. Ultrasound obtained on admission. Digital cervical examinations were avoided for the remainder of the pregnancy.

Hospital course:
Long antepartum stay. Bleeding settled with observation. Labetalol 200 mg BID continued throughout.
02/18: blood pressures and lab criteria met for preeclampsia superimposed on her chronic hypertension.
02/25 (32w5d): while on IV magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis she became short of breath with palpitations. BP 150/100, HR 88, RR 22. Lethargic, DTRs absent, shallow respirations. ABG 7.35 / pCO2 45 / pO2 95. Lytes: Na 138, K 4.2, Cl 100, HCO3 24, Ca 8.9. Mg 5.2 mg/dL (high). Magnesium infusion stopped; calcium gluconate 1 g IV given. Over the next hours she became alert and reflexes returned. Mg 2.4 the following morning.
03/06 (34w1d): repeat low transverse cesarean. Liveborn infant. Uncomplicated postoperative course.

Discharge diagnoses: pregnancy delivered by repeat cesarean at 34w1d; preeclampsia superimposed on chronic hypertension; magnesium toxicity (hypermagnesemia), resolved; antepartum bleeding with digital cervical exam contraindicated.

Discharge medications: labetalol 200 mg PO BID; prenatal vitamin with DHA daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks for BP; OB postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u.

Admitted 1/22 at nearly 28 wks for painless bleeding, stayed on the antepartum unit until delivery. Developed superimposed preeclampsia 2/18. On 2/25 had magnesium toxicity on the mag drip - Mg 5.2, lethargic, absent reflexes - drip stopped, calcium given, recovered by the next day (Mg 2.4). Repeat C-section 3/6 at 34w1d. Discharged 3/10. Summary received and reviewed.

Today: tired but ok. Baby came home on Sunday. Incision healing. Home BPs 128-142 / 82-92. No headache, visual symptoms, RUQ pain or dyspnea. Mood ok, a lot of support at home. On labetalol 200 BID and prenatal.

Exam: BP as charted. Alert, comfortable. Lungs clear, heart RRR. Incision clean, dry, intact. Trace ankle edema, no more. DTRs 2+ symmetric.
PHQ-9 5.

A/P
1. Chronic HTN, postpartum - slightly above target but improving trend at home. Continue labetalol 200 BID. Labs today. Home log, recheck at OB 6 wk visit and here in summer.
2. Preeclampsia, delivered - resolved. Added history of preeclampsia; important for any future pregnancy.
3. Magnesium toxicity - resolved; repeat Mg today.
4. Postpartum mood - screen low, reviewed warning signs.
Pregnancy items closed out on the problem list.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tiana - blood counts, kidney and liver tests and magnesium are all back to normal. Keep up the home blood pressure log and send me readings in 2 weeks.

Postpartum visit 04/24/2024

7 weeks after repeat cesarean at 34w1d (course complicated by superimposed preeclampsia and magnesium toxicity, both resolved).
BP 130/84 on labetalol 200 mg BID. Incision well healed. Lochia resolved. Mood good.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: HTN check. Back at work part time since June. Baby thriving. Home readings 124-134 / 78-86. Takes labetalol morning and night, occasionally late with the PM dose. Walking with the stroller most evenings. No side effects - no dizziness, no fatigue beyond the usual with an infant.
O: BP as charted. Wt down about 3.5 kg since March. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: Chronic hypertension, controlled. Continue labetalol 200 BID. If she wants to stay off another pregnancy for a while and BP stays good we can revisit the regimen, but no change now. BMP today. Obesity - weight trending down, encouraged. Fall shots in October. RTC 6 mo for physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

34 yo. Feels well. Baby is 10 months, sleeping better. Working full time again. BP log steady, high 120s to mid 130s over low-mid 80s. Still on prenatal daily - she and her husband would like another child at some point but not yet. Labetalol 200 BID, no missed doses she can recall.

ROS negative except mild fatigue.

Exam: BP as charted. NAD. HEENT normal, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed incisions. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions; Pap/HPV obtained. Extremities without edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-9 2.

A/P
- Chronic HTN: controlled on labetalol. If she plans pregnancy, labetalol is fine to continue; told her to message me as soon as she has a positive test so we can coordinate with OB early, given her preeclampsia history.
- Class I obesity: weight a little lower than summer. Continue walking.
- Screening: Pap with HPV today. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin. HIV/HCV already done 2023. Flu and COVID done in October.
- RTC 3 months BP.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - OBSTETRICS / OB INTENSIVE CARE
Admitted 01/09/2026   Discharged 01/13/2026

35 yo G3P2 at 34w0d with chronic hypertension and prior superimposed preeclampsia, admitted 2024 for antepartum bleeding. Presented with new pain in the right upper abdomen and nausea that would not settle. Had felt more tired over recent days with little appetite.

On arrival BP 148/96. Mild scleral icterus. Tender in the RUQ. Reflexes brisk, symmetric. Fetal tracing reassuring.
Labs: platelets 74,000/uL; AST 290; ALT 235; total bilirubin 3.1; LDH 680; haptoglobin undetectable. Urine protein 2+.

Assessment: severe preeclampsia, HELLP form, superimposed on chronic hypertension.

Course: stabilized in OB intensive care. Magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis. Repeat cesarean the same day (third cesarean). Liveborn infant. Magnesium continued 24 hours postpartum, then stopped. Labs improved steadily; on 01/12 platelets 146, AST 52, ALT 66, bilirubin 0.9.

Discharge diagnoses: severe preeclampsia (HELLP) superimposed on chronic hypertension, delivered by repeat cesarean at 34w0d.
Discharge medications: labetalol 200 mg PO BID; prenatal vitamin with DHA daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: BP check in OB clinic within a week; postpartum visit 6 weeks; primary care for ongoing BP.

documents.title: Emergency Department and Readmission Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT / OBSTETRICS
Dates of service: 01/16/2026 - 01/18/2026

One week after cesarean (01/09) for severe preeclampsia. Came in after home BP readings were high. ED BP 150/100, HR 88. OB consulted; readmitted for postpartum preeclampsia and IV magnesium sulfate started for seizure prophylaxis. Labetalol 200 mg BID continued.

Overnight on the infusion she reported trouble breathing and felt weak all over. Exam: lethargic; patellar reflexes absent; breath sounds diminished at both bases, no wheeze or crackles; RR 12.
ABG: pH 7.35, pCO2 50, pO2 70.
Na 138, K 4.2, Cl 100, HCO3 24, Ca 8.9. Mg 5.2 mg/dL (elevated).

Impression: magnesium toxicity with hypoventilation.
Magnesium stopped. Calcium gluconate 1 g IV. Alert with reflexes back within a few hours; Mg 2.6 in the morning.

Discharged 01/18 on labetalol 200 mg BID and prenatal vitamin. NKDA. BP check in OB clinic in 3-4 days, then routine postpartum care. Recommend PCP follow-up for blood pressure.

documents.title: Update and refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I had the baby on the 9th, early again, and then ended up back in the hospital for my pressure a week later. Long story, they should be sending you the paperwork. Both of us are home and doing ok. Could you send a refill of the labetalol? I'm down to a week. I'll make an appointment once things calm down a little.

documents.title: RE: Update and refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tiana, so glad you and the baby are home. Labetalol 200 mg twice a day sent to your pharmacy. The hospital records came in this morning and I'm reading them. Keep checking your pressure and follow the OB plan; any reading of 160/110 or more, a severe headache or trouble breathing means going straight back in. Book with us whenever you're ready.
